description: Quarterly enterprise risk review for the board risk committee of a regional commercial bank.
provenance: Modeled on regulated bank board risk packs: risk-appetite indicators, criticized-loan trends, liquidity and capital, operational incidents, scenario analysis, and committee decisions. Deliberately exercises an eight-slide deck with a four-series bar chart, red/amber/green narrative encoded as status prose, and dense control-remediation detail.

content.title: Q3 2026 Enterprise Risk Review
content.subtitle: Board Risk Committee | October 21, 2026 | Confidential supervisory information

content.title: Risk is within appetite; office CRE and vendor resilience need action.
content.subtitle: Chief Risk Officer assessment
prose: Credit migration slowed and liquidity buffers strengthened in Q3.
Office CRE is the only metric outside appetite; three credits totaling $184M moved to criticized.
No material cyber loss occurred in Q3.
The July processor outage exposed a recovery gap; parallel routing is requested.

content.title: Criticized balances are stabilizing outside downtown office
content.subtitle: Special mention, substandard, and nonaccrual loans by portfolio, $M

content.title: Downside scenario — resilience versus vulnerability
content.subtitle: Nine-quarter supervisory-style stress using a 5.8% unemployment peak and 24% office-value decline

content.title: Operational, cyber, and third-party risk
content.subtitle: Material incidents and control health through September 30, 2026
bulletPoints: Payment processor outage on July 18 disrupted debit authorization for 96 minutes; customer losses were $0.4M and fully reimbursed
Processor recovery-time objective missed by 51 minutes; remediation due November 15 with weekly evidence review by Technology Risk
One ransomware event at a payroll vendor exposed employee names and bank-routing details for 312 current and former employees
Phishing click rate improved to 2.1% from 3.4%; privileged-access recertification closed with 17 stale accounts removed
Model inventory includes 84 tier-one and tier-two models; two CECL overlays remain beyond validation due dates
Internal audit rated branch cash controls satisfactory and vendor concentration governance needs improvement

content.title: Open remediation and accountable owners
content.subtitle: Items rated high or overdue
bulletPoints: Parallel debit-routing design — CIO — decision today; implementation by March 2027; estimated spend $3.2M
Office CRE concentration plan — Chief Credit Officer — reduce exposure-to-capital below 155% by June 2027
CECL overlay validation — Head of Model Risk — first overlay by November 30; second by January 31
Third-party fourth-party inventory — Chief Procurement Officer — complete critical-vendor mapping by December 15
Identity governance recertification automation — CISO — pilot complete; production rollout February 2027
Resolution planning data lineage — CFO — 7 of 9 critical reports remediated; final two due December 31

content.title: Approve parallel debit routing and extend the office CRE exception.
content.subtitle: Agenda items 3 and 4
prose: Quarterly reporting resumes once exposure-to-capital falls below 155%.
Criticized office balances must also decline for two consecutive quarters.
